item.title: 49ers pivoted to Keenan Allen trade after initially focusing on Josh Downs
item.description: The 49ers made a trade for wide receiver Keenan Allen on Tuesday, but he wasn't the only Colts wide receiver on their radar ahead of the trade deadline.
item.content:encoded:
The 49ers made a trade for wide receiver Keenan Allen on Tuesday, but he wasn't the only Colts wide receiver on their radar ahead of the trade deadline.

During a Thursday appearance on KNBR, General Manager John Lynch said that the team turned its attention to Allen after initially targeting Josh Downs as an addition to their receiver room. Lynch said that head coach Kyle Shanahan brought up Allen while watching film on Downs and conversations with the Colts began before they landed defensive tackle DeForest Buckner in an earlier deal with Indianapolis.

"We kind of focused on Josh Downs as an option that we'd have some interest," Lynch said, via 49ersWebzone.com. "And Kyle and I are kind of watching Josh, and in the process, Kyle's like, 'Man, what about Keenan?' And I was like, 'You know, we hadn't given much thought to that, but let me ask about that.' And so, there started a conversation about two and a half weeks ago, really, when the DeForest talks [happened]. 'Would he?' And it's always fluid, and at a certain time, they didn't want to give up Keenan. It kind of wasn't going to be on the table, but we kept communicating, and ultimately we got him."

The 49ers sent a 2027 sixth-round pick to the Colts for Allen. Downs and a 2027 seventh-round pick were eventually traded to the Chiefs for 2027 fourth- and fifth-round picks.

item.title: What to know about Falcons – Chiefs in Week 10
item.description: This is a tough one for a skidding Falcons team.
item.content:encoded:
The Atlanta Falcons are about to get their bye week, but they have to go through the Kansas City Chiefs first. The difference between rolling into the bye at 3-7 with the Vikings and Lions looming after it and being a 4-6 in the same boat is a potentially significant one, given that the NFC South is extremely weak and Atlanta’s final five games are against the Browns, Commanders, and their division rivals.

But winning this game is going to be difficult, and more difficult for trading away Jessie Bates. Can our beloved Falcons stop being so thoroughly mediocre and triumph over an AFC juggernaut? For better or worse, we’ll find out.

Here’s what you need to know about the Week 10 matchup.

Team rankings

That’s a big gulf!

The Falcons, by the eye test, the more advanced statistics, and the high level ones I share every week here, are a 3-6 football team that looks like a 3-6 football team. By all those same measures, the Chiefs are one of the ten best teams in football. If this isn’t an ass kicking—and especially if the Falcons actually win—it will be a real triumph.

How the Chiefs have changed

This team is a diminished version of the Chiefs that briefly ruled the NFL. That’s not to say that Kansas City is not still a contender—they are—or that they aren’t still one of the best teams in the AFC. It is to say that they’re no longer a juggernaut.

They did re-imagine the offense by signing Kenneth Walker to a massive free agency deal, and Walker’s been one of the handful of great running backs in the league this year. Before this, the Chiefs had relied on a hodgepodge of lackluster backs, so the lift he’s given them has helped offset a still-frustrating passing game. The team also acquired Justin Fields to back up Patrick Mahomes, and there’s a non-zero chance we’ll see Fields this week with Mahomes banged up. Eric Bieniemy is also back in the offensive coordinator role, and the offense has been noticeably better balanced than it has been in recent years.

Their draft has delivered plenty of needed young talent, even if the production has been mixed to this point. Mansoor Delane looks excellent but has only appeared in five games, defensive linemen R Mason Thomas and Peter Woods have real promise even if Woods has largely struggled, Jadon Canady is providing surprisingly strong coverage at cornerback early in his career, and running back Emmett Johnson and wide receiver Cyrus Allen have produced in their limited opportunities to this point. It’s a good class that could pay real dividends down the line.

Finally, the Chiefs made a bit of a splash trade, grabbing wide receiver Josh Downs from the selling Colts. Downs is not a standout but has been a consistently productive player on some lousy Colts teams, and is now joining up as a clear top option for Mahomes once he gets his feet under him in Kansas City.

Generally, though, you know what this Chiefs team looks like. Andy Reid is the coach, Mahomes is the quarterback, the receivers are all varying degrees of frustrating, and stalwarts like Travis Kelce and Chris Jones are still puttering along at an impressively high level. The Chiefs are still very good because of that, but they’re better health and more cohesion away from being a great team.

What to know about Week 10

So much swings on whether the Falcons will see Patrick Mahomes or not. Justin Fields can kill Atlanta with his legs and avoids turnovers, but there’s a massive drop-off from Mahomes to him that will impact an already inconsistent Chiefs passing attack.

That’s important because of what Joe Burrow and Caleb Williams have done to the Falcons’ secondary, which is now down a playmaking presence in Bates. Both quarterbacks annihilated Atlanta’s coverage with sharp ball placement, good throws on the move, and effective movement in the face of pressure, and Mahomes can manage all that. The chief (sorry) difference here is that while the Bengals have Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins and the Bears brought Colston Loveland, Rome Odunze, and Luther Burden to bear (sorry again), the Chiefs have a much more lackluster collection of playmakers. Their most effective option by far is Rashee Rice, who is always seemingly banged up but is lethal over the middle of the field, and Travis Kelce remains a plodding but useful receiving threat. Downs is an intriguing new addition, but how much time he’ll see less than a week after being traded to Kansas City remains to be seen. If the Falcons can do a reasonable job of bottling those three up, Xavier Worthy is thoroughly mediocre and their fourth best receiving option is probably Walker, who is dangerous in the open field but not a threat downfield.

I targeted the passing game first here because of the intrigue around Mahomes vs. Fields, but the single biggest threat in this game is Walker. The Falcons were eaten alive by the Bucccaneers ground game two weeks ago, and Walker is the most dangerous back they’ll face all season. He’s 7th in the NFL in success rate, second behind Bijan Robinson in rushing yards by a measly eight yards, has yet to fumble once, and is averaging more yards per game than any other back in football. Atlanta’s run defense has been exposed as a mediocre one over the past month, and the threat of the Chiefs simply running over this unit can’t be exaggerated. Walker may get 25 carries if he’s rolling, and if he’s rolling, the Falcons are in major trouble.

Unfortunately for an Atlanta offense that has been a real puzzle box the past couple of weeks, the Kansas City defense is no pushover, either. They’re doing a nice job of limiting explosive plays and are top ten in counting stats, success rate, and EPA defensively against the pass and the run, underscoring how fundamentally sound they are. A sloppy version of this Falcons offense is going to run into trouble, and a sloppy version of this Falcons offense is all we’ve gotten lately. Your best bet is going to be to run outside where the Chiefs are marginally less stout, and I’m sure Bijan Robinson has no problem with that plan. If everyone’s blocking well, the Falcons should at least be able to get a toehold on the ground.

Things through the air are going to be tougher. We don’t know how Corey Levin is going to hold up full-time as the starting center, but we do know it’s a tough matchup against this Kansas City interior, and that Michael Penix Jr. has both struggled under pressure and faced way too many quick pressures in recent weeks. The Chiefs have the talent at every level to punish Penix locked in on receivers, Levin struggling against pressure, and Atlanta’s pass catchers not getting separation. If the past two weeks of woes continue, this one could get out of hand.

One item to watch this week if the game is close? Atlanta has a new kicker and the Chiefs are sticking with Harrison Butker, who has been abysmal this season. If Jake Moody can keep rolling, as he has over the past couple of seasons, and Butker struggles, a 3-6 point game could swing on kickers.

Overall, though, I’m going to follow my own advice and urge you to do the same: Don’t expect the Falcons to win a game against a superior opponent, and hope for the best.

item.title: NFL predictions: Our picks for Giants-Commanders, the full Week 10 slate
item.description: BBV staff has confidence in the Giants.
item.content:encoded:
The New York Giants and Washington Commanders kick off Week 10 of the NFL season Thursday night at what promises to be a rainy, chilly MetLife Stadium. Can the Giants solidify their NFC East lead, or will the race for the division title tighten? Here is how the Big Blue View staff sees that game, and the rest of the Week 10 matchups.

Chris Pflum

Which version of the Giants will show up on Thursday night?

Will we get the sloppy Giants that came out flat against the Philadelphia Eagles, or the tough, physical, and technically sound Giants that showed up against the Houston Texans? John Harbaugh’s 9-1 record home record on Thursday Nights is encouraging.

I would say that this is a game the Giants should win on paper, particularly with Washington missing some of their best players and their starting center in the concussion protocol. However, I’m also not convinced that these Giants can play a normal game and just take care of business. I keep waiting for the Giants to play a complete game and execute on offense and defense, but this team seems unable to be both consistent and explosive.

I hope the offensive line comes prepared to bully an injured Washington defensive line and J.J. McCarthy isn’t forced into low percentage throws every third down by long yardage situations. Likewise, I hope that Dennard Wilson comes out swinging on defense, but also has a counterpunch ready in case Jayden Daniels has an answer to the Cover-0 blitz.

I’m picking the Giants here, but they can’t afford to take Washington lightly or give Jayden Daniels the chance to catch his breath and swing the game.

Pick: Giants

Tony Del Genio

This is the Giants’ second consecutive must-win game. You wouldn’t think that when 5-2-1 plays 2-5-1, but (1) the Giants haven’t beaten the Commanders since Jayden Daniels became their quarterback (even though Daniels didn’t play in one of those losses), (2) despite their record, Washington has beaten the Seahawks and only narrowly lost to the 49ers and Rams while the Giants were beaten soundly by the Rams, the only good team they’ve faced, and still have the 49ers and Seahawks coming up, along with the Jaguars and Lions. A division loss greatly weakens their hold on the NFC East lead, their only real path to the playoffs.

Terry McLaurin is out for the season, but in his place is Stefon Diggs, who did not face the Giants in the first game. Jacory Crosky-Merritt, who beat the Giants’ run D for a 33-yard TD right off the bat in the first game, is also out. The Commanders are further decimated by injuries since their last meeting to key starters such as DT Daron Payne and IOL Lucas Patrick. So really the Giants should prevail. The problem is…containing the running of Daniels, which they did not do well in their first meeting (103 yards, by far his highest of the season, and his only 2 rushing TDs of the season). Hopefully Dennard Wilson will have a plan for that. If so, and if the Giants execute it, then the Giants can win.

Pick: Giants

David Hartman

The rematch of the NFL’s only tie game of the season will be played in prime time on Thursday night, and for the ninth time in nine games, the Giants are playing a team that doesn’t have a winning record. But you can throw the records out the window: The 5-2-1 Giants, at home, are just 1.5 point favorites over the 2-5-1 Commanders. Go figure…

Big Blue won with defense and a strong kicking game on Sunday in Philadelphia, with Arvel Reese perhaps becoming a star in real time. It was an ugly win, with the offense producing just 19 points. The Giants will need more than that against Jayden Daniels and company on Thursday night. Cam Skattebo is expected back, and that’s good news. New York couldn’t run the ball on Sunday, which stagnated their offense. Right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) might miss this game, however, and the O-line struggled at Philadelphia as it was.

J.J. McCarthy wasn’t terrible on Sunday, but he wasn’t especially good either and now he’s dealing with a hip pointer. Jameis Winston led New York on its only touchdown drive while
McCarthy was temporarily knocked from the game. McCarthy hasn’t thrown a TD pass (or an interception) in either of his two starts.

This figures to be a close game, just like the first one. It’ll be fun to watch standout rookies Reese and Sonny Styles — college teammates at Ohio State last season — leading the way for each defense. Seriously – how did anyone score on the Buckeyes? Anyway, Dennard Wilson needs to find a way to keep Daniels from gashing his defense with his legs. He ran for 103 yards and two scores in the first game.

This game could come down to intangibles like turnovers and special teams. The G-Men have been winning (or tying) close games and that’s a reflection on good coaching to a degree, and favorable luck. In a game that should be close, who am I to pick against that?

Pick: Giants in a squeaker

Valentine’s View

We are not picking games by the spread here, but I am surprised the Giants are just 1.5-point favorites. That indicates a continuing lack of real belief in the Giants in the betting market. The Giants understand the opportunity they have in front of them, and how important this game is.

In the rainy, windy, miserable conditions at MetLife Stadium Thursday evening I think you have to expect what has become a typical Giants game this season — close, somewhat sloppy, decided by who makes the plays and who properly handles the situations at the end of the game.

I have far more faith in the Giants to do that than I do the Commanders.

We all remember the Commanders stunning clock mismanagement at the end of the Week 5 tie with the Giants. That sort of questionable decision-making has continued to plague Washington, which is 1-3-1 in games decided by one score.

If you could the Arizona game, which I do since it was decided on the game’s final play, seven of the Giants eight games this season were one-score games. The Giants are 5-1-1 in those games. They have lived on the edge, and have shown an ability to survive.

Is that formula sustainable forever? Maybe not. It does, though, make me feel good about the Giants’ chances on Thursday.

Pick: Giants

item.title: AFC North Preview, Week 10: First place on the line between the Steelers and Bengals
item.description: Updated Standings: Cincinnati Bengals Matchup: vs. Pittsburgh Steelers, 8:20pm EST The Bengals avoided a potential letdown game last week against the Atlanta Falcons in Spain, securing a 34-17 victory. After losing the first quarter by three points, the Bengals outscored the Falcons by 20 points for the remainder of the contest. Now riding a four-game […]
item.content:encoded:
Updated Standings:

  1. Pittsburgh Steelers 6-2
  2. Cincinnati Bengals 6-2
  3. Cleveland Browns 5-4
  4. Baltimore Ravens 4-5
Cincinnati Bengals

Matchup:vs. Pittsburgh Steelers, 8:20pm EST

The Bengals avoided a potential letdown game last week against the Atlanta Falcons in Spain, securing a 34-17 victory. After losing the first quarter by three points, the Bengals outscored the Falcons by 20 points for the remainder of the contest. Now riding a four-game win streak, having exceeded 30+ points in each game, the Bengals will return home for a primetime matchup with the Steelers.

In Week 3, the Bengals suffered a 30-27 defeat against Pittsburgh and sit in second place now despite having the same record. Cincinnati’s passing attack has been firing on all cylinders recently and Joe Burrow is hitting his stride. Over the last four games, Burrow has 16 touchdown passes while averaging over 300 passing yards. The Steelers are a Top 3 defense against the run but rank middle-of-the-pack defending the pass. The Bengals continue to struggle running the ball effectively, so they’ll likely attack Pittsburgh’s secondary regularly.

Elsewhere, the Bengals’ inconsistent run defense may be tested by Steelers’ rushing attack that has totaled 148 yards and 200 yards on the ground in back-to-back games. The Bengals will need to slow down Jaylen Warren in the backfield, who has been a star this season. If the Bengals can make the Steelers one dimensional offensively, they become a much more beatable team.

Pittsburgh Steelers

Matchup:vs. Cincinnati Bengals, 8:20pm EST

Like their divisional counterpart, the Steelers have won their last four games to improve to 6-2, sitting atop the division by virtue of tiebreaker. Prior to last week’s bye break, the Steelers defeated the Browns handedly by 21 points, their most lopsided win of the season and only their second win by more than one possession. Pittsburgh’s momentum will be put to the test in a tough road environment this Sunday night with the AFC North lead on the line.

The Steelers have won the turnover battle in three consecutive games. That will be an important factor for them to defeat the Bengals. Burrow has taken good care of the ball this year but did have a three-interception performance just two weeks ago. If the Steelers’ defense can force a turnover or two and give their offense support with shorter fields, that will go a long way in helping them keep pace.

On offense, the Steelers continue to long for better production from their pass-catchers to help unlock more downfield plays. Warren has been the team’s only consistent playmaker and Rico Dowdle has ran well over the last two weeks in a complimentary role. However, D.K. Metcalf and company have been up-and-down in the passing game. In order to match Cincinnati’s high-flying offensive attack, the Steelers will likely need to hit on a few explosive passing plays.

Cleveland Browns

Matchup: vs. Houston Texans, 1:00pm EST

The Browns have now lost back-to-back games and are looking to get back on track before their upcoming bye week. In Week 9, they allowed a winnable game to slip through their grasp against the Saints, where they lost by one point in overtime. Shedeur Sanders impressed in his spot-start for Deshaun Watson at quarterback, but the Browns still struggled to run the ball and didn’t start scoring much until the fourth quarter.

Watson is set to return from injury to start this week versus his former team. The Texans have underwhelmed defensively this year but still have one of the league’s more talented defenses, which will pose a challenge for the Browns — whose offense has struggled mightily at times this season. Houston has been vulnerable in pass coverage, allowing over 235 passing yards per game, leaving some hope that Watson can hit a downfield shot or two. The Browns will need to connect on some type of explosive plays or find a way to run the ball more effectively.

Defensively, the Browns will need to bring their A game, as the Texans have prolific offensively at times in recent weeks. Last Sunday, they scored 44 points and C.J. Stroud threw five touchdown passes with nearly 400 passing yards. The Browns may be able to afford to sell out against the pass rather than the run, as the Texans rank even worse running the ball than they do.

Baltimore Ravens

Matchup:vs. Los Angeles Chargers, 8:15pm EST

The Ravens were thrashed by the Jacksonville Jaguars last Thursday night, losing by 20+ points for the third straight game. Baltimore’s offense struggles hit a new low, as the team scored 10 points, gained 10 first downs and totaled just over 200 yards. With a hobbled third-string quarterback under center, the Ravens were no match for a talented Jaguars’ squad. Fortunately, they will get the ultimate potential get-right matchup this coming Monday, taking on a winless Chargers team that is in disarray.

Hopes for a potential offensive turnaround lie with new incoming quarterback Jacoby Brissett, who the Ravens traded for after Week 9. Brissett should provide a significant upgrade over Joe Fagnano as an experienced veteran who has proven, at the bare minimum, he can lead scoring drives and operate an offense at a competent level. Even with Brissett now under center, the Ravens need more consistency from their offensive line and breakthrough performances from veterans like Mark Andrews, Ronnie Stanley and Derrick Henry.

Defensively, the Ravens have given up 30+ points in three straight weeks to three of the best offenses and quarterbacks in the NFL. They’ve played good halves and quarters, but the lows have been low. Coverage breakdowns and lack of impact pass rush continue to plague them. If there were ever a spot to have a convincing performance and force turnovers, this would be it. Chargers’ quarterback Justin Herbert leads all quarterbacks in interceptions this season.

item.title: Bengals designate Andrei Iosivas, two others for return from IR
item.description: The Bengals will have three players back at practice on Thursday.
item.content:encoded:
The Bengals will have three players back at practice on Thursday.

They announced that they have designated wide receiver Andrei Iosivas, cornerback Jalen Davis, and guard Brian Parker for return from injured reserve. All three players will be able to practice with the team for the next 21 days and they can return to the active roster at any point in that window.

Iosivas has been out since Week 2 with a thumb injury. He had three catches for 19 yards in the first two weeks of the season and had 69 catches over the previous two seasons.

Davis played in the first three games and has been out with a hamstring injury. He had five tackles, a tackle for loss and a pass defensed before his injury.

Parker was a sixth-round pick this year and landed on injured reserve ahead of Week 1.

Week 10 begins the second half of the NFL regular season. With the playoff picture beginning to take shape in both conferences, every matchup carries added importance as teams look to leapfrog one another in the standings.

There are plenty of intriguing matchups, potential upsets, and opportunities for teams to make statements this weekend. With 7 divisional battles, Week 10 features several games that could go either way. Which teams will come through, and which teams are starting to fade? Let’s break down every matchup and make our Week 10 NFL picks.

My Week 10 Picks

(Bye: Chicago Bears, Denver Broncos, Philadelphia Eagles, Tampa Bay Buccaneers)

Washington Commanders @ New York Giants — Thurs., 8:15 p.m. ET

Jayden Daniels simply does not have enough of a supporting cast in 2026 to be competitive. The Commanders defense will get better with the presence of Sonny Styles.

The only reason this game will be close is because the Giants are working with JJ McCarthy / Jameis Winston at quarterback.

My Pick: Giants 26-20

New England Patriots @ Detroit Lions — Sun., 9:30 a.m. ET (Munich)

The Patriots were embarrassed by the Packers. Jared Goff will not have the same type of field day but Jahmyr Gibbs will be the focal point that gets the Lions the win.

My Pick: Lions 24-20

I don’t think I will ever pick the Jets to win a game.

My Pick: Bills 38-17

Carolina Panthers @ New Orleans Saints — Sun., 1:00 p.m. ET

The NFC South plays itself. The Panthers are the more complete team but traveling to New Orleans could present challenges.

My Pick: Panthers 31-28 (OT)

Houston Texans @ Cleveland Browns — Sun., 1:00 p.m. ET

The Texans will start their second half ascension to threaten the Patriots for the AFC’s 7th seed.

My Pick: Texans 24-13

Jacksonville Jaguars @ Tennessee Titans — Sun., 1:00 p.m. ET

I hope the Jaguars represent the AFC this year. They made some splash moves and they have a great opportunity to earn the #1 seed with a weak AFC South.

My Pick: Jaguars 33-14

Kansas City Chiefs @ Atlanta Falcons — Sun., 1:00 p.m. ET

I could see this being a trap game for the Chiefs who have to slow down Bijan Robinson. Meanwhile, the Falcons must win with a 3-6 record and being 4th in the division.

My Pick: Falcons 24-20

Miami Dolphins @ Indianapolis Colts — Sun., 1:00 p.m. ET

Jeff Hafley might be starting to get more out of the defense in Miami after holding the Patriots to 24 points and the Lions to 19 points. The Colts have made it known that they are punting on the 2026 season.

My Pick: Dolphins 28-25

Minnesota Vikings @ Green Bay Packers — Sun., 1:00 p.m. ET

Even though the Vikings have Kirk Cousins in place to help the offense, I think the Packers defense is playing good football. Not to mention that their passing offense is the best in football right now.

My Pick: Packers 27-18

Seattle Seahawks @ Las Vegas Raiders @ Sun., 4:05 p.m. ET

Klint Kubiak gets to face off against this former team with rookie quarterback – Fernando Mendoza. Mike Macdonald will make it a point of emphasis to rattle the rookie signal caller. I’m willing to bet he throws 3 interceptions in this one or takes 5+ sacks.

My Pick: Seahawks 24-6

Los Angeles Rams @ Arizona Cardinals — Sun., 4:05 p.m. ET

The Rams need this game to get a divisional win (improving divisional record) and move themselves to 4-2 in NFC games. Doing so, would put more pressure on Minnesota, Green Bay, and Seattle.

My Pick: Rams 23-9

San Francisco 49ers @ Dallas Cowboys — Sun., 4:25 p.m. ET

Dallas’s defense is about to get worked.

My Pick: 49ers 37-27

Pittsburgh Steelers @ Cincinnati Bengals — Sun., 8:20 p.m. ET

A pretty good Sunday Night Football game on tap. Aaron Rodgers travels to Joe Burrow and the Bengals with first place in the AFC North on the line. The Bengals get this one since its a home game.

My Pick: Bengals

Los Angeles Chargers @ Baltimore Ravens — Mon., 8:15 p.m. ET

The Jesse Minter game. Jacoby Brissett tries to lead a win over the winless Chargers. Minter should know how to attack Justin Herbert.

My Pick: Ravens 20-17

item.title: The Steelers made zero trades – and that’s completely fine
item.description: The Steelers didn’t make a trade, and that’s completely fine.
item.content:encoded:
I don’t want to talk out of both sides of my mouth here. When the NFL trade deadline came and went, I was vocal with my praise of the Jacksonville Jaguars for their “F—k them picks” approach and pushing all their chips to the middle of the table.

Many Pittsburgh Steelers fans were hopeful that general manager Omar Khan would make a big move(s) of his own after the Steelers were at the center of trade rumors for the better part of a month. Instead, Pittsburgh stayed put and didn’t make any trades before the 4:00 PM EST deadline on Tuesday, which led to many a Steelers fan to all but proclaim the season as over.

I don’t know how I became the rational one as it pertains to the Steelers, but the front office not making any sort of trade doesn’t bother me in the slightest. Would I have enjoyed seeing a big-time safety like Amani Hooker or Jessie Bates head to Pittsburgh? Yes. The same can be said about a cornerback like Riq Woolen or Charvarius Ward. At the same time, though, the defense is phenomenal. They are fourth in fewest points per game allowed, seventh in yards per game, and their run defense has been the best in the NFL since Week 4. I’m all for a great unit getting even greater, and would have loved a trade for any of the aforementioned names, but I’m also not throwing my hands in the air about it.

As it pertains to the receiver position, there were simply no needle-moving trades to be made. Brian Thomas Jr. was the golden goose and best available name at the position – the Jaguars opted to keep him, and that was probably the right move on their part. Who else were the Steelers supposed to try and get? Josh Downs isn’t a needle mover. Calvin Ridley certainly isn’t, either. They’ll get Michael Pittman and Roman Wilson back in the lineup before the end of the season, which will provide in-house aid to the group of pass-catchers.

Yes, I love when a team goes balls to the wall and puts everything on the line to win a championship. I mentioned the Jaguars, and they are a perfect example of that. However, they are also in a very different position than Pittsburgh organizationally. They have a long-term answer at quarterback signed and locked up in Trevor Lawrence who is continuing where he left off in 2025 when he finished fifth in MVP voting. They have a group of three-five legitimate pass-catchers at receiver and tight end and a good run game. They are the only team in the league that is currently top five in offensive and defensive EPA. And while the Steelers are in the midst of a great season themselves, they don’t have that long-term answer at quarterback on the roster, making them (understandably) hesitant to part ways with draft picks to use in a potential trade up in the 2027 NFL Draft to select a signal-caller.

So with that all in mind, let’s focus on the rest of 2026. What does the offense need to do going forward after keeping their group the exact same? For starters, spend more time under center. The Steelers are the 10th-best offense in terms of EPA since Week 4 when they go under center. Additionally, keep trotting out heavier personnel. Over that same time span, Pittsburgh is the best team in the NFL when they have three tight ends on the field. Bully ball is working. They need to lean into it more rather than try to make a largely ineffective passing game the star of the show.

There are plenty of things we can be hard on the Steelers’ front office and ownership for. The trade and extension for DK Metcalf, then following that up with trading away George Pickens. item.title: NFL Thursday Night Football preview: Commanders try to put previous nightmare vs. Giants behind them
item.description: The Commanders and Giants had a memorable tie in their first meeting.
item.content:encoded:
The Washington Commanders should have had a win over the New York Giants this season. Or at least a field-goal attempt for the win.

The last time the Commanders and Giants played, it ended with one of the worst game-management fiascos in recent years. The Commanders were in line for a game-winning 42-yard field goal in overtime. Then it got weird. Washington was painfully slow in running a play from scrimmage in the final minute; Jayden Daniels inexplicably allowed himself to be tackled, and time ran out before Washington could spike it. The game ended in a tie with Washington never getting that field-goal attempt.

The Commanders can't get the play off in time and this game ends in a tie pic.twitter.com/WmPp6q5hU0

— NFL (@NFL) October 11, 2026

Washington is 1-2 since then, and its record this season is a disappointing 2-5-1. The Giants, gifted a half-win in Washington, are 2-1 since then and 5-2-1 overall, good for first place in the NFC East.

The Giants aren't a dominant team, but they're in a great position to win the division and host a playoff game. If the season ended now, they'd be the No. 3 seed in the NFC. Acquiring J.J. McCarthy for a fifth-round pick has had a big impact on their season (and the Vikings' season too). McCarthy isn't coming off his best game — Jameis Winston led the Giants' only touchdown drive in a 19-11 win over the Eagles last week — and is dealing with a hip pointer, but overall he has shown some promise.

The Commanders have been a mess most of the season, and Daniels rightfully said after last week's loss to the Rams that the Giants game is a "must-win." They can't afford a loss. Or even a half-loss like they took when these teams met the first time.

Who needs it more?

The Commanders' season is practically over, and Dan Quinn's job status might be in jeopardy with a loss on Thursday. If Washington loses, it would be four games behind the Giants and New York would own the tiebreaker. There wouldn't be much reason for hope if that happens. But if the Commanders win, they'd be just two games back and have the tiebreaker. That's a massive swing. The Giants want to get this win to practically eliminate the Commanders and move closer to an NFC East title, but Washington is clearly the more desperate team.

Key player: Giants WR Malik Nabers

Malik Nabers came into the season with some questions over his health, as he was coming off a torn ACL. But over the first half of the season, he has re-established himself as one of the top young receivers in the NFL. He has 53 catches for 648 yards, and that is after a pretty slow start. He had four 100-yard games in a row, a streak that was snapped last week. In the first meeting with the Commanders, Nabers had 11 catches for 121 yards and a game-tying touchdown with 1:43 left in regulation. The Commanders do not have a cornerback who can reasonably match up with Nabers. Washington is 30th in passing yards allowed and 28th in passing touchdowns allowed. If they can't contain Nabers, it could be a long night.

Betting market watch

The New York Giants have a sizable lead in the NFC East and have also been one of the most reliable teams for bettors to back this season (6-2 against the spread). It wasn't pretty, but J.J. McCarthy, Jameis Winston & Co. won (and covered) on Sunday against the Eagles. Although McCarthy left the game briefly with a hip injury, it appears he'll play.

On the other sideline, the Commanders had yet another late-game blunder in a 20-13 loss to the Los Angeles Rams in Week 9. Washington is going nowhere fast, and the team has a lot more questions than answers at the moment. It's a little surprising this spread is only New York -2.5, but it's also hard not to back Big Blue at under a field goal. — Ben Fawkes

Check out more of Ben's work at the Yahoo Sports betting hub.

Fantasy football storylines

The Giants and Commanders played an adorable tie game five weeks ago, with both teams frittering away a likely win in overtime. Thursday night, they get the anticipated rematch. Here are three fantasy themes to track as you watch the game.

1. Will Malik Nabers go off again? Nabers had a four-game streak of 100-yard efforts snapped last week, but this is a great chance to get cooking again. He drew 20 targets and posted an 11-121-1 return the last time he faced Washington's beatable secondary.

2. Can Jayden Daniels get his running mojo back? Daniels needs to run proactively to be at his best, and he gashed the Giants for 103 yards in that prior meeting. He's had just 49 yards rushing, total, in his last three starts. The Washington pass-catchers are ordinary, so if Daniels is going to be a fantasy-worthy start here, he needs to use his athleticism.

3. Is Cam Skattebo back in the Circle of Trust? It's been a whirlwind sophomore year for Skattebo — fumbles, injury, a soft benching. And the Giants did kick the tires on a Jonathan Taylor trade this week. Alas, Skattebo is someone they probably need, given how poorly Devin Singletary played against the Eagles. The Washington run defense has been solid all year, a stark contrast to the pass defense. — Scott Pianowski

I have no explanation for the last two weeks. But I'll use an unexpected run of success to provide a warning to anyone else who wakes up one day in the midst of a hot streak.

In Week 8, I went 13-1 in the straight-up-only picks exercise. (No more picks against the spread, for reasons I've previously explained.) For Week 9, I ended up 14-1.

That's 27-2 over two weeks. (Which translates to 87-48-1 for the year, which doesn't sound nearly as good as "27-2.")

Now for the warning, specifically to anyone who has gambled or who will be gambling on sports. The worst thing you can do is get lucky. Because you'll think that you've suddenly become good.

Then, you'll let it ride until your luck runs out. That's when it gets dangerous. Because you'll fool yourself into thinking that it's just a temporary setback, that your secret formula for picking winners remains viable, and you'll chase your losses. You'll keep digging that hole, confident that it's just a matter of time before your sudden genius returns.

Eventually, you'll find yourself in an untenable financial situation.

That's how it happens for plenty of gamblers. They don't start out losing and keep losing. They win enough to make themselves think they know more than they do, when the reality is that no one knows anything. And then the wheels come off. And then they get desperate to put the wheels back on.

Case in point: Last week, someone who has been part of the NFL universe for more than 30 years expressed amazement that the Cowboys were favored by only 4.5 points against the Colts. With the Colts in disarray due to multiple trades and poised to make even more trades, the Cowboys would win easily. It was, the person said, a "sure thing."

Final score? Cowboys 27, Colts 23.

There is no sure thing in gambling. Well, there's one. If you ever let yourself believe you're smarter than the house and you don't snap out of it in time, it's a sure thing that you'll be filing for bankruptcy, eventually.

item.title: Patriots have ‘all the belief in the world’ in Christian Gonzalez
item.description: Gonzalez and the Patriots defense struggled against the Packers last week.
item.content:encoded:
The Green Bay Packers had their way with the New England Patriots secondary in Week 9, and one player more than any other was in the spotlight afterwards. Being the closest defender on multiple big plays, Christian Gonzalez was the poster boy for his team’s 45-27 defeat.

Despite the performance, however, the Patriots are not hitting the panic button. Instead, their belief in the 24-year-old remains unshaken.

“Obviously, Christian had a couple of plays that he’d definitely want back,“ said defensive coordinator Zak Kuhr ahead of Thursday’s practice in Munich. “But there are some things that fans don’t see or people don’t see that might not be on Christian, but he happens to be around the ball. And sometimes the blame comes with that.

“But we know what Christian’s capable of and we have all the support and belief in him in the world.”

According to charting by Next Gen Stats, the Patriots’ No. 1 cornerback became the first defender since at least 2018 to give up 80-plus receiving yards to two different players in one game against the Packers. Overall, the Patriots defense allowed Green Bay’s receiving duo of Christian Watson and Matthew Golden to beat them for a combined 17 catches for 335 yards and a pair of touchdowns.

With a Detroit Lions team on the dock more than capable of putting pressure on a defense itself, the Patriots and Gonzalez in particular will need a quick turnaround. According to Kuhr, however, the start was encouraging.

“I don’t want to do any predictions or anything like that, but I thought we had a really good day of practice yesterday,“ he said. “There was good energy. There was good execution. There was improvement in communication, some connection in the back end it was exciting to see. There was some good energy out there. I think the guys were excited to get back to work, like, ‘Let’s get this thing right.’”

item.title: Arrowhead Pride Midseason Awards: The Chiefs’ Protector of the Year
item.description: Three Kansas City linemen drew votes for Arrowhead Pride’s midseason offensive line award.
item.content:encoded:
There are eight games in the books — with nine more to go. The Kansas City Chiefs’ 2026 season reaches its midpoint in Week 10. Because the team’s bye came so early in Week 5, we have decided to move our annual awards to midseason.

Nine members of the Arrowhead Pride writing staff each had one vote for our seven midseason awards, so nine votes will be tallied for each award.

So far, we’ve awarded:

Most Improved Player: DB Chris Roland-Wallace

Top Defensive Rookie: CB Mansoor Delane

In this post, we’ll reveal our top offensive lineman so far.

RG Trey Smith

VOTING: Trey Smith (5), Kahlil Benson (2), Creed Humphrey (2)

The NFL now gives out the “Protector of the Year” award, so we will too. Right guard Trey Smith is the winner at the midseason point, playing 506 of 510 possible snaps and starting in all eight games.

The Chiefs’ run game has been revitalized this year, and Smith has been a key factor in the push up front. Kansas City ranks 10th in ESPN’s run-block win rate (74%), despite two games in which starting left guard Kingsley Suamataia was benched.

The Chiefs rank 12th in pass-block win rate as a unit, and Smith does not grade as highly in pass blocking as Humphrey or Suamataia, according to ESPN, but Smith has allowed just seven pressures (two quarterback hits and five hurries) over 307 pass-blocking snaps; Suamataia has allowed seven pressures (one sack, three hits and three pressures) in just 221 pass-blocking snaps, according to Pro Football Focus.

The intensity Smith brings is the cherry on top of his reliable presence on the line. He isn’t a perfect blocker, but he’s been Kansas City’s most consistent offensive lineman in a season where the unit’s depth is already being tested.

Center Creed Humphrey’s low snaps likely hurt his chances at winning the poll, but rookie left tackle Kahlil Benson deserved some love; he has played every snap possible at left tackle this season.

Is Smith the Chiefs’ top offensive lineman so far this year? Let us know in the comments.

item.title: Cowboys vs 49ers: 2 players Dallas should use more in Week 10

item.content:encoded:
Fresh off a thrilling 27-23 victory over the Indianapolis Colts, the Dallas Cowboys return home on Sunday to host the red-hot San Francisco 49ers. If the Cowboys want to record their first winning streak since last November, they’ll need to bring their A-game against one of the league’s best teams.

Before the two teams square off on Sunday, here are two players the Cowboys should use more in the matchup.

1) EDGE James Houston

One pain point for Dallas’ defense this season has been their inability to consistently take down the opposing quarterback. While the Cowboys defense is tied for fifth in the league in pressure rate (32.8%), they have accumulated only 17 total sacks as a team, tied for the sixth-fewest.

One change the Cowboys made in the past few weeks to help their struggling pass rush group was activating 27-year-old edge Jame Houston for their last three matchups. Houston, who played just 13 defensive snaps before Dallas’ Week 8 matchup against Arizona, made a big impact in his first outing with increased opportunities. 

In that game against the Cardinals, Houston recorded two pressures and a sack on just 11 pass-rush snaps. The former sixth-round pick had a 27.3% win percentage in that contest, the highest of any Cowboys defender, to go with a PRP of 13.6. 

After an impressive performance, Dallas rewarded him with more chances against the Colts. Houston played a season-high 31 defensive snaps with 18 pass-rush opportunities. While the 27-year-old couldn’t quite replicate his pass-rush success from a week prior, he recorded a 69.3 pass-rush grade on true pass sets, with a 12.5% TPS win percentage.

If the Cowboys want the best chance to improve their pass rush, they need to keep increasing Houston’s usage on defense. Dallas should give Houston some of Donovan Ezeiruaku and Von Miller’s snaps to see if he can continue his upward trajectory.

2) S Alijah Clark

The Cowboys defense got some unfortunate news after Sunday’s win. Safety P.J. Locke suffered a concussion and has already been ruled out for this week’s matchup against the 49ers.

If the Cowboys are going to continue to play Caleb Downs primarily in the slot, Downs played 35 snaps there on Sunday; they’ll need someone to replace Locke as their second primary safety. Dallas’ coaching staff has shown an affinity for giving Markquese Bell chances when they had injuries to both starting safeties early in the year, but given how poorly Bell has performed, it’s time to give Alijah Clark the nod.

Clark played 40 defensive snaps against the Eagles a few weeks back, allowing just one catch for nine yards in coverage. While Clark may not be as sure of a tackler as Bell, he is without a doubt more skilled in coverage. Dallas should give Clark the job to start alongside Malik Hooker and see if he can perform better than Bell has.

item.title: NFL Picks Week 10: When Everybody’s First… Nobody Is
item.description: Week 9 proved to be a week with some thrilling finishes. Let’s take a look at all of the action coming up in Week 10.
item.content:encoded:
The New Orleans Saints host the Carolina Panthers this Sunday with first place in the NFC South on the line, for one week anyway. We can all honestly admit that we are in a continuing five-year loop of the NFC South being an absolutely terrible division. Since 2022, no NFC South Champion has ended the season with less than seven losses, and this season should certainly keep that sad distinction intact. This season could easily see the division champ sport double-digit losses.

As it stands, New Orleans and Carolina, at 3-5 respectively, are playing for sole possession of first place, but there is still a lot of season to go, and Sunday’s winner will still have Tampa Bay and Atlanta to contend with as well. This may very well feel like the consolation prize division, but a title is a title, and the home Wild Card game that is awarded to the winner will be gladly taken all the same. Let’s take a look at this and all of the exciting Week 10 action in the NFL.

Last week I went 14-1!

I told you so: Saints over Browns!

What do I know: Patriots over Packers?

***

WEEK 10

Thursday, November 12th – Thursday Night Football

Commanders(2-5-1) at Giants(5-2-1)

The last time these two met, it ended in a tie. This time, New York gets the win and all but wins the NFC (L)East. New York wins 27-21.

Pick: Giants

***

Sunday, November 15th – Very Early Game

Patriots(5-4) at* Lions(6-2) – Munich, Germany

Detroit gets a fifth-consecutive win, with a scrappy effort in Germany against the Pats, who are still stinging from last week’s beating against the Pack. Detroit wins 20-14.

Pick: Lions

***

Sunday, November 15th – Early Games

Chiefs(6-2) at Falcons(3-6)

Kansas City rebounded from their two-game skid with a dominant performance last week, and they will continue to roll here against the floundering Falcons. Kansas City wins 21-13.

Pick: Chiefs

***

Texans(3-5) at Browns(5-4) 

Following a dominant road win last week, Houston will get another here, over the overrated Browns in Cleveland. Houston wins 35-24.

Pick: Texans

***

Vikings(6-2) at Packers(6-3) – Game of the Week

After an effort that set offensive football back to the Stone Age on Monday Night, Minnesota broke open the emergency glass to brink Kirk Cousins back to the Twin Cities. This NFC North clash for first place will be a slugfest, but Cousins and company will find a way to win. Minnesota wins 20-16.

Pick: Vikings

***

Dolphins(1-7) at Colts(2-7)

Indy is currently on a five-game losing streak, but they get just what they need to stop the slide, a matchup with Miami. Indianapolis wins 24-9.

Pick: Colts

***

Bills(7-1) at Jets(2-7)

Buffalo’s fantastic season will continue its trajectory with an impressive win over the Jets. Buffalo wins 33-9.

Pick: Bills

***

Jaguars(6-2) at Titans(1-7)

The re-tooled Jags will dominate the Titans in Tennessee. Jacksonville wins 33-6.

Pick: Jaguars

***

Panthers(3-5) at Saints(3-5)

Someway, somehow, the Saints find themselves battling for the NFC South lead, and of all the teams they should face for that distinction, Carolina might just be the ideal opponent, as Kellen Moore and Tyler Shough are undefeated against Bryce Young’s Panthers. This one, just like every single New Orleans Saints victory you’ve watched all season, will come down to the very last play. A Charlie Smyth game-winning field goal on the final play is the difference in this fight to the top of the NFL’s smallest mountain. Saints win 23-20.

Pick: Saints

***

Sunday, November 15th – Late Games

Rams(5-4) at Cardinals(3-6)

The Rams will win their fourth-consecutive game by winning against the last team to beat them, Arizona. Los Angeles wins 33-19.

Pick: Rams

***

Seahawks(5-4) at Raiders(4-5)

The Fernando Mendoza era in Las Vegas begins with a tough draw, the reigning Super Bowl Champion Seahawks. The Silver and Black will fight valiently, but ultimately lose. Seattle wins 30-21

Pick: Seahawks

***

49ers(7-1) at Cowboys(4-5)

This once-heralded rivalry will continue to be dominated by the Niners, who will win their fifth-straight against Dallas. San Franciso wins 29-16.

Pick: 49ers

***

Sunday Night Football

Steelers(6-2) at Bengals(6-2)

Both of these AFC North rivals are riding high on four-game winning streaks, as the winner of this game takes first place in the division. Pittsburgh won the first matchup this season, but Cincy will take the rematch at home. Cincinnati wins 32-24.

Pick: Bengals

***

Monday, November 16th – Monday Night Football

Chargers(0-8) at Ravens(4-5)

When this matchup was made during the offseason, it was a no-brainer primetime showdown. Today, not so much. The spiraling Ravens are on a four-game losing streak that can only be snapped by facing the worst team in the NFL, the pitiful Chargers. Baltimore wins 28-13.

Pick: Ravens

***

There you have it, Week 10 is upon us. Leave us your picks, comments, and insight below!

item.title: NFL Injury Report, Week 10: Latest news, updates for Puka Nacua, George Pickens, more players for fantasy football
item.description: We go over the Week 10 NFL Injury Report, providing the latest updates and news, plus fantasy football analysis.
item.content:encoded:
It's the halfway point of the 2026 NFL season and by now you likely have weathered plenty of injuries on your fantasy football rosters. We have a handful of big names we're tracking going into Week 10 while four teams are on bye — the Bears, Broncos, Buccaneers and Eagles. Below we'll update you on the latest injury news, plus provide some useful fantasy football analysis.

Quarterback

  • Patrick Mahomes, KC (elbow)

  • Sam Darnold, SEA (quad/ribs) — Out for Week 10

  • Drew Lock, SEA (oblique) — Should be good to start

  • Justin Herbert, LAC (finger)

  • Deshaun Watson, CLE (concussion) — Set to start

  • Malik Willis, MIA (groin) — Placed on IR

  • Gardner Minshew, ARI (elbow) — On IR with torn UCL

Mahomes: At the time of Mahomes' injury in Week 9, it looked as though we were watching a QB who may be done for the season. But after exiting due to an elbow injury, Mahomes was able to return in the Chiefs' 35-12 win over the Jets on Sunday. Mahomes completed 23-of-31 passes for 242 yards and two scores, posting fewer than 20 fantasy points for the fifth time in the past six games.

Kenneth Walker III continues to be the focal point of the offense as the passing game lacks depth and a vertical threat. The Chiefs face the Falcons in Week 10 and Mahomes was a full practice participant Wednesday, a good sign for him being able to play. If he's able to go, it'll be a chance for him to work with new receiver Josh Downs, who came over in a trade with the Colts on Tuesday.

Seahawks QBs: Head coach Mike Macdonald already went on the radio Monday and said Darnold will be out Week 10 against the Raiders. Lock underwent tests on an oblique injury he suffered Sunday and those came back "good," so he's in line to start again. The Raiders have been a great fantasy matchup for QBs this season, allowing the fifth-most points to the position. However, the Seattle offense has struggled a bit with lack of depth behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Lock is back in the QB2 streaming convo for Sunday and isn't a bad spot start if you have Caleb Williams or Bo Nix on bye.

Minshew: The Cardinals QB is on IR with a torn UCL. That means rookie Carson Beck will start. If you remember back to the preseason, Beck was actually pretty good. There's a chance this is a good move overall for the offense, particularly TE Trey McBride. But Arizona is down WR Michael Wilson (neck) and Beck won't have many other options in the passing game. In Superflex, Beck is worth a speculative add to see how he does in Week 10 against the Rams.

Willis: The Dolphins surprised us before the trade deadline by placing Willis on IR, which could mean he's done for the season this late in the year. He'll miss at least the next four games, which would mean the soonest he could be back is Week 14 against Chicago. 2025 sixth-round pick Kyle McCord is the backup and will start in Week 10 versus the Colts. Brady Cook will be the backup.

Miami's passing offense enters Week 10 ranked 30th in the NFL. Chances are it doesn't get much better with McCord under center, but we'll need to see. It's a downgrade to receivers like Malik Washington, Greg Dulcich and Caleb Douglas in the short term until we assess things. Ollie Gordon II could be leaned on a bit more, and McCord may use the RB and Dulcich as safety valves.

Running Back

  • Rhamondre Stevenson, NE (knee)

  • TreVeyon Henderson, NE (illness — ruled out)

  • Woody Marks, HOU (Knee)

  • Josh Jacobs, GB (finger) — Report: Out a max of three weeks

  • Travis Etienne Jr., NO (hamstring) — Chance to return this week

  • Bhayshul Tuten, JAX (ankle/foot) — DNP on Wednesday

Patriots RBs: Stevenson exited Sunday's blowout loss to the Packers early and did not return. Henderson has missed the past two games after being hospitalized due to "unexplained neurological symptoms." Stevenson missed practice Wednesday and will reportedly be sidelined multiple weeks. The Patriots face the Lions in Germany this week, which means Corey Kiner is likely to take over as the lead back. He finished with a solid 8-55-1 rushing line against Green Bay, though most of that production was on a fourth-quarter drive when the game was essentially over. Lan Larison would be the RB2 for New England.

Jacobs: On the other side of that game, Jacobs suffered a fractured finger in the win over the Patriots and didn't return. Rushing duties were then split between Pierre Strong Jr. and Kaleb Johnson with MarShawn Lloyd out. Johnson rushed for 68 yards on 14 carries with a score. He looked pretty good running the ball for a team that has struggled to do so all season. But it was also in a blowout. Even so, Johnson is a proactive add off the waiver wire with Jacobs expected to miss time. Green Bay faces the Vikings in Week 10 before the bye and it would be hard to trust any Packers RB against one of the best defenses in the NFL. Johnson will be a risky flex play against Minnesota in Week 10. Strong isn't a bad add in deeper PPR formats and keep an eye on Lloyd, who could be back soon.

Wide Receiver

  • Puka Nacua, LAR (knee/turf toe) — To miss "significant" time

  • Michael Wilson, ARI (neck) — Out for season

  • Luther Burden III, CHI (concussion) — on bye

  • Ladd McConkey, LAC (back) — Day-to-day

  • Jaylen Waddle, DEN (concussion) — on bye

  • Xavier Worthy, KC (hamstring)

  • George Pickens, DAL (hamstring)

  • Mike Evans, SF (Achilles)

  • DeVonta Smith, PHI (hamstring)

  • A.J. Brown, NE (knee)

  • Carnell Tate, TEN (shoulder)

  • Deebo Samuel Sr., SF (hamstring)

  • Garrett Wilson, NYJ (concussion)

Nacua: Sean McVay told reporters Wednesday that the wideout will avoid IR for now but miss "significant" time with knee sprains and turf toe. The Rams are already without Davante Adams, but McVay did offer hope that the veteran WR could return from a ruptured hamstring as soon as Week 13. For now, there isn't much WR depth. Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell and the trio of tight ends — Tyler Higbee, Colby Parkinson and Davis Allen — will need to step up. We'd throw Terrance Ferguson into that group, but he remains on IR and isn't expected back in Week 10. L.A. should lean more on its run game with Kyren Williams and Blake Corum.

With Nacua out, it's a downgrade to the passing game and Matthew Stafford's fantasy outlook. It's a slight bump up for Williams and Corum, both of whom are involved in the passing game plenty. The Rams take on the Cardinals before their bye in Week 11, which is an easy draw for the run game. Mumpfield isn't a bad waiver wire add, along with Atwell in deeper formats. But don't expect any receiver to get the type of volume like Nacua did.

Michael Wilson: The WR will miss the rest of the season due to a neck injury. It's a tough blow for managers who were hoping for more following the Marvin Harrison Jr. trade. Instead, Wilson struggled, failing to reach double-digit fantasy points in four of the past five games. With Jalen Brooks and Kendrick Bourne on injured reserve, Arizona is very, very thin at WR.

Simi Fehoko, Reggie Virgil and Devin Duvernay all played significant snaps in Week 9 against Seattle. None of them did much, while Trey McBride was obviously the main target for Gardner Minshew. Though, Minshew is on IR with a torn UCL and the team will start rookie Carson Beck at QB this week.

Pickens: The Cowboys held Pickens out of their win over the Colts in Week 9. As a result, CeeDee Lamb went off for 10-195-1 while third-string WR Ryan Flournoy was quiet with two catches for 53 yards. Dallas leaned on the run game, leading most of the first half. It's clear the offense missed Pickens and will need him ready for a key NFC matchup with the Niners in Week 10. Pickens was a limited practice participant Wednesday. item.title: Daniel Jones responds to Colts offloading talent at trade deadline: 'You're not happy to see it'
item.description: Daniel Jones hated to see the Colts sell off talent at the trade deadline.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL trade deadline came and went Tuesday and the Indianapolis Colts exited the day as the team that offloaded the most talent. After trading both Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner in the days before the deadline, the team also offloaded wideouts Josh Downs and Keenan Allen on deadline day.

One player who didn't get moved was quarterback Daniel Jones. After seeing the extent of his team's selloff, Jones admitted he wasn't super happy about the Colts' new direction, per Fox 59.

"Honestly, you're not happy to see it, right?'' he said Wednesday. "You're a player and you're going out there competing and doing everything you can to win games. So, you're not happy to see a lot of those decisions.

"But . . . it's outside of our control and our job is to play and be prepared to play well. We've got a lot of trust in the guys coming into those spots and we'll be ready to go.''

It's tough to blame Jones for feeling that way. Following those moves, the Colts' most productive wide receiver is now Laquon Treadwell. He's caught 16 passes for 215 yards in nine games this season.

The options on the depth chart behind Treadwell aren't exactly proven commodities. Nick Westbrook-Ikhine is the only other wide receiver on the roster — along with Treadwell — who has at least 100 career receptions. The other three receivers on the Colts' roster — Deion Burks, Ashton Dulin and Anthony Gould — have combined for just 54 career receptions.

It's now up to Jones to make the most of that unproven group.

That could prove challenging. Jones struggled to build on last year's breakout even with Allen and Downs in the lineup. Through nine games, Jones has just six touchdowns against 10 interceptions. He's faced questions about his job security, though he received backing from head coach Shane Steichen.

Despite Jones' struggles, there were some rumors suggesting he could be traded at the deadline. Jones was linked to the Minnesota Vikings, who were desperately in need of a quarterback after backup Carson Wentz struggled in Week 9. Jones had familiarity with the Vikings, as he spent a portion of the 2024 season with the team following his release from the New York Giants. Ultimately, the Vikings decided to bring back veteran Kirk Cousins in a trade with the Las Vegas Raiders.

If it's any consolation for Jones, the Colts did retain his biggest playmaker. Running back Jonathan Taylor was not traded at the deadline, and should continue to be the focal point of the Colts' offense. Jones also still has tight end Tyler Warren, who is now the team's leading pass catcher. Overall, though, it's not the most encouraging group.

The writing has been on the wall for both Jones and the Colts for multiple weeks now. With the quarterback failing to match last year's success, the team's offense cratered. The Colts responded appropriately, selling off short-term parts for long-term help.

That may prove to be the smartest thing for the team in the long run, but it's going to make Jones' job significantly harder in 2026.

item.title: Longtime Steelers player, coach Dick Hoak dies at 86
item.description: The Steelers announced the death of their longtime player and coach Dick Hoak at the age of 86.
item.content:encoded:
The Steelers announced the death of their longtime player and coach Dick Hoak at the age of 86.

Hoak was born outside of Pittsburgh and went to Penn State before the Steelers made him a 1961 seventh-round pick. He spent 10 years as one of the team's running backs and finished his career with 3,965 rushing yards and 1,452 receiving yards. Hoak scored 33 overall touchdowns during his time on the roster.

Hoak joined Chuck Noll's staff as an offensive backfield coach in 1972, moved to running backs coach in 1991 and was the only one of Noll's coaches who remained on the staff under Noll's successor Bill Cowher. He retired in 2006 after coaching future Hall of Famers Franco Harris and Jerome Bettis and being part of five Super Bowl champions.

"We are deeply saddened by the passing of Dick Hoak, a legendary member of the Pittsburgh Steelers family," Steelers owner Art Rooney II said in a statement. "Dick was part of the foundation of this organization and played an instrumental role in shaping the Steelers as both a player and coach during his 45 years with the team. Dick represented everything the Steelers stand for with his toughness, loyalty, dedication and an unwavering commitment to the team. First as a player, then as a coach, Dick's contributions to this organization spanned generations."

Hoak is a member of the Steelers' Hall of Honor and received the Pro Football Hall of Fame's Award of Excellence in 2025.

item.title: Fantasy Football Start 'Em, Sit 'Em: Need help for the flex spot in Week 10? Joel Smyth has you covered
item.description: Fantasy football analyst Joel Smyth examines the flex range of players for Week 10.
item.content:encoded:
We're on to Week 10 of the fantasy football season! As we look for every advantage this season, the X-factor position is the FLEX. To break it all down, analyst Joel Smyth goes through eight players in the consensus rankings flex zone for your flexes, double flexes, or even third WR slots.

​Set & Forget

Blake Corum vs. ARI

Blake Corum has been a top-20 fantasy RB in five consecutive weeks as his role continues to eat into Kyren Williams' workload. Even so, he's being ranked outside the top 20 in the consensus … versus an Arizona defense? In this economy?

The Cardinals, led by Carson Beck and Reggie Virgil, are 10-point underdogs at home. Over the last month, Corum has been best when the Rams control the game and avoid obvious passing situations, which gives him a healthy amount of volume even as an RB2. He'll be listed as an RB2 on the depth chart, but he should be treated as if he's a team's starter in fantasy football.

Ollie Gordon II vs. IND​

The passing attacks in this matchup may set the game back a generation. The good news is Ollie Gordon II should be set up to see a lot of rushing volume against a bottom-five RB defense in Indianapolis. Miami is in the rare spot where, although it is starting a sixth-round QB with zero game experience in Kyle McCord, it is only a three-point underdog on the road. That's what happens when a team sells everyone at the deadline the way the Colts did. The Dolphins should be able to keep this one close and ride their RB on the ground.

Flex Starts

DJ Moore vs. NYJ

I believe Moore is being a little bit underrated because of last week's low output and his early-season injuries. First off, everyone struggles against Minnesota. I've found it best to trash those games from my mind completely for fantasy's sake. Second, Moore's volume has been quietly impressive when healthy, actually ranking eighth-best on a per route basis.

He's had two games where he's left early, but when he's on the field, he's being targeted plenty by one of the best quarterbacks in the NFL on a top-five offense. The game script may not be in his favor here, but Moore should be able to capitalize early to return FLEX value.

Jalen Coker vs. NO

For a short while, Coker was too good for this article, but he's back in style this week after a disappointing stretch. Coker is a volume WR, and that should play out well on Sunday when the Panthers (the fastest-paced team in the NFL) play the Saints (the second-fastest-paced team in the NFL). It's a game projected to be close, high-scoring and the Panthers will face a defense that ranks bottom-five versus wideouts this season. If Carolina can protect Bryce Young from Chase Young and company, Coker should be able to produce on his volume much better than the last few weeks.

Double Flex Only

Jordan Addison vs. GB

Kirk Cousins is a Viking, and Justin Jefferson is saved! But what about Jordan Addison? Well, in the first eight games of his NFL career, the only eight with Cousins, Addison averaged 15.8 PPR PPG, and 12.8 when Jefferson was available! If this were 2023 again, you'd be confused as to why he is in the double-flex section. Well, less confused this year, as Addison has failed to be fantasy relevant, but I believe he can pay off in deeper leagues this week with the addition of Cousins and the absence of Carson Wentz. The touchdown potential alone boosts his value tremendously. Cousins' final game in Minnesota was against the Green Bay Packers, when the rookie Addison was targeted eight times, bringing in seven receptions for 84 yards and a TD.

Corey Kiner vs. DET

A starting running back on a good offense that isn't being played in most leagues is rare. I believe Kiner should be getting more love. The receiving role isn't there, but the Detroit Lions’ rushing defense has benefited from the schedule so far, as the "third-ranked RB defense" is actually 14th versus rushing fantasy points when adjusted to the RBs they've faced. With Stevenson and Henderson out, Kiner is the clear trusted RB in an offense that has averaged the second-most offensive points since Week 4. Kiner had the red-zone touchdown run last week and we're hoping for another one to come overseas.

Booby Traps​

Tyler Allgeier vs. LAR​

It isn't just that Carson Beck is making his first career start, but that the Cardinals offense is without every single starting WR, Allgeier's running mates and their left tackle. Everybody's hurt … except for Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett on the other side. You can't score points if you can't stay on the field, and I worry mightily about the Cardinals offense being able to do just that. Allgeier and the other Cardinals can always score in garbage time to return FLEX numbers, but I don't love banking on that unless you're truly desperate.

The Rams' run defense already ranks top-five this season versus fantasy RBs and grades out as one of the biggest OL-versus-DL run advantages of the week, even with their star players missing games to start the year.

Jakobi Meyers vs. TEN

Meyers is ranked inside the top-30 WRs this week, which is understandable given the Titans defense and the team dealing players away at the deadline. However, that same thing can work against him. Meyers has run 33 routes in the fourth quarter this season … that is less than Brandin Cooks. He can hit if he finds his way into the end zone, but in comparison to Parker Washington, Meyers is much more volume-reliant, making less big plays after the catch and near the end zone. He still only had three of eight games with over four targets this season and will need Cam Ward to help him out on Sunday against Jacksonville's new and improved defense.

The NFL trade deadline was a busy one as clubs made moves to shore up weak spots. Several of those deals were made in part to combat troublesome injuries that had weakened the teams' overall depth.

The newcomers will likely need an adjustment period with their new teams while the bumps and bruises heal elsewhere.

Let's turn our attention to some of the most prominent players' ongoing injury issues that will impact fantasy managers most in Week 10. As always, keep an eye on the latest developments leading up to kickoff with our player notes page.

ON BYE: Chicago, Denver, Philadelphia, Tampa Bay

WEEK 10 RANKINGS:QB | RB | WR | TE | K | DST | FLEX

QB Patrick Mahomes, Kansas City Chiefs

Mahomes was a full participant in practice on Wednesday, Nov. 11 after hurting his elbow late in the first half of Sunday's game against the Jets when he was hit in the middle of his throwing motion. An MRI earlier in the week revealed an elbow strain/sprain, but no structural damage.

QB Deshaun Watson, Cleveland Browns

The Browns announced Wednesday that Watson (concussion) will start on Sunday against the Texans. He had previously cleared the protocol last Saturday, but didn't have enough time to prepare for the Week 9 game against the Saints. Shedeur Sanders started and threw for 297 yards and two touchdowns. Watson has been one of the most-often sacked quarterbacks in the NFL, so it's probably best for fantasy managers to steer clear of this game − unless they have the Texans defense.

RB Bhayshul Tuten, Jacksonville Jaguars

Tuten (ankle/foot) did not practice on Wednesday, but that shouldn't be any reflection of his eventual status for Sunday against the Titans. He was limited last week as well before suiting up against the Ravens. However, he only played 20 snaps and rushed for just 29 yards on 12 carries, though he did salvage a decent fantasy day by scoring a touchdown. Backup Chris Rodriguez is also dealing with a hand injury, but he did manage a limited practice on Wednesday.

More: Fantasy football Start ‘Em, Sit ‘Em: 30 players to start or sit in Week 10

RB Cam Skattebo, New York Giants

Skattebo hasn't played since suffering a hamstring strain in Week 7 against the Texans, but he'll be good to go on Thursday night vs. Washington. He was a full participant in practice Tuesday and Wednesday, which is good news for a Giants offense that got a whopping 31 yards on 21 carries from Devin Singletary last week.

RB Travis Etienne, New Orleans Saints

Currently on injured reserve with a hamstring strain, Etienne was spotted at practice on Wednesday. He might not be ready to play on Sunday, but the team could activate him soon. If he's available in your league, it might not be a bad idea to make a preemptive claim. He'll need to be activated by 4 p.m. ET on Saturday to be available against the Panthers.

WR Garrett Wilson, New York Jets

Wilson sat out last week's game with a concussion, but returned to practice on a limited basis on Wednesday. That's a step in the right direction, but it may not be enough to get him on the field this Sunday against the Bills. Look for Wilson to be a game-time decision.

WR A.J. Brown, New England Patriots

Brown has played in just three games this season, the last one coming in Week 7 before his problematic knee started acting up. He also missed four games earlier in the year with an ankle injury that may not be fully healed. He was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, so he's making some progress. The Patriots have already said Brown will make the trip to Germany for this week's game against the Lions. DeMario Douglas has stepped forward in Brown's absence, with a touchdown catch in Week 8 and five receptions for 102 yards last week.

WR Ladd McConkey, Los Angeles Chargers

Does anyone really know what McConkey's status is these days? He was declared active last week before kickoff, but didn't play any snaps due to ongoing back spasms. Coach Jim Harbaugh said McConkey is day-to-day, but even if he does make it back to practice this week, he's still a very risky start with the Chargers playing on "Monday Night Football." Find another option.

TE Hunter Henry, New England Patriots

Henry suffered a foot injury in Week 8 and was questionable to play last week. He gutted it out and caught three passes for 35 yards. Considering the Patriots depleted receiving corps, he should be a primary target for QB Drake Maye. However, Henry was also outsnapped by fellow tight end Eli Raridon in Week 9, 35-31. The rookie finished with three catches for 52 yards.
